identity.title: Reasoning as Representation: Rethinking Visual Reinforcement Learning in Image Quality Assessment

problem.claim: Explain why reinforcement-learning-trained reasoning-based IQA models generalize well and how to retain that capability with lower deployment cost.

gap.claim: The mechanisms and critical factors underlying these models’ generalization remain underexplored.

contributions.claim: The authors report that RL training converts redundant visual representations into compact, cross-domain-aligned text representations, identifying this conversion as the source of observed generalization.
RALI uses contrastive learning to align images directly with the generalizable text representations learned through RL, avoiding reasoning processes and loading an LLM.

stated_novelty.claim: The paper proposes RALI as a direct image-to-generalizable-text alignment approach that removes the need for reasoning during inference and for an LLM.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments supporting the interpretation that RL-trained MLLMs perform the visual-to-compact-text conversion described above.
The authors report that RALI achieves quality-scoring generalization comparable to reasoning-based models while using less than 5% of their model parameters and inference time.

narrative_sequence.summary: Reasoning-based RL IQA models show exceptional generalization, but their mechanisms are insufficiently understood.
Their inference energy use and latency are reported to be orders of magnitude higher than those of earlier models.
Experiments are reported to link generalization to conversion of redundant visual representations into compact, cross-domain-aligned text representations.
RALI directly aligns images with those text representations, removes reasoning and LLM loading, and reportedly preserves comparable generalization at under 5% of the parameters and inference time.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects a costly capability to an intermediate representation and then designs a method that targets that representation directly.

lessons.interpretation: Making the proposed mechanism explicit can guide efficiency interventions more precisely than reproducing the full original computation.
lessons.application: When presenting an efficiency method, identify the representation associated with the target capability and align the cheaper model directly to it.
lessons.exception: This move is unsuitable when the intermediate representation is not observable, learnable, or sufficient for the task.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, baselines, exact energy or latency measurements, or experimental protocols.
The meaning of “comparable” generalization and the scope of “cross-domain” alignment are not quantified.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported mechanism or performance.
